implemented: Explicit manual/auto validation across compile, daemon startup/reload and Herdr launch binding.
Manual leaves provider defaults and explicit provider arguments/options in control. Auto maps Codex task approvals/sandbox and Claude permission mode at process/session launch.

Generated permission options remain outside persisted declarative configuration; reload to manual has no generated argv residue. Codex manual reload test supplies explicit on-request/read-only options.
Conflicting command-line/config/protocol permission overrides are rejected; Herdr auto declarations require matching actual launch arguments.
Required role command surfaces cannot silently run as advisory prompts: unsupported native enforcement follows fail_mount. The same check runs before regular task input and on reload.
Malformed ordinary live-role resources retain task-local failure/recovery semantics under manual mode; auto requires readable role metadata and does not echo invalid manifest contents.

limits: Native hard enforcement of role command allowlists and managed role tools is still unimplemented; required policies fail mount rather than being weakened.
Pi has no supported native auto-permission switch and is rejected for that explicit mode.
Manual means no CCB-generated automatic override; it does not revoke explicit user provider settings or independently prove the effective policy of every restored provider session.
Legacy bypass-hook-trust/project acceptance behavior, inherited permissions, provider dialogs and finer caller authorization still require parity/acceptance work.
